builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Replaces summarization, masking, and structured or embedding-based memory with an append-only plain-text history log and a regex search tool for on-demand recall. Costs storage of the full unabridged history, extra tool-call latency and prompt tokens per search, and, in the paper's setup, reinforcement learning on the agent model to teach effective grep usage. Can fail when relevant facts cannot be matched by literal patterns (paraphrased or implicit information), when logs grow large enough to make searches noisy or expensive, or when an untrained model issues poor queries and under-retrieves.
rationale: An append-only log plus a regex search tool requires no embeddings, index, or extra models and fits constrained infrastructure, but the reported results come from an RL-trained 9B agent, so the gain must be re-validated with the reader's own model or API before production reliance.
technique: Append-only text log with regex grep recall

claims.statement: Replaces summarization, masking, and structured or embedding-based memory with an append-only plain-text history log and a regex search tool for on-demand recall. Costs storage of the full unabridged history, extra tool-call latency and prompt tokens per search, and, in the paper's setup, reinforcement learning on the agent model to teach effective grep usage. Can fail when relevant facts cannot be matched by literal patterns (paraphrased or implicit information), when logs grow large enough to make searches noisy or expensive, or when an untrained model issues poor queries and under-retrieves.

95-97% accuracy on ContextBench versus at most 21% for lossy baselines, and +8.8 percentage points over SUPO summarization on BCP-Multi; positioned on the accuracy-token-cost Pareto frontier across five tasks.
